I was not informed of the reason for the closure, nor did I receive any written notification from the bank. This has caused significant financial inconvenience, as I have been unable to access my remaining balance or transfer the funds to another account. 

As a consumer, I am entitled to protection under both Missouri law and federal regulations regarding the closure of my account and access to my funds. Specifically, I believe the following laws are relevant to my case : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  Account Closure Laws Under Missouri Revised Statutes 362.410, a bank has the right to close an account, but must do so in accordance with the terms of the account agreement. Generally, a bank is required to provide reasonable notice of account closure, particularly if the closure results in the account holder being unable to access their funds. Failure to notify a customer, as is the case in this instance, may be in violation of this law.

2. Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E The Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq., and Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. Part 1005, govern electronic fund transfers, including withdrawals, deposits, and other transactions involving consumer accounts. Under these laws, a financial institution must provide clear information about the closure of an account, as well as ensure that the consumer has access to their remaining funds. If an account is closed and there are funds remaining, the bank is required to facilitate the withdrawal or transfer of those funds promptly.

3. The Right to Access Your Funds Under Missouri law, when a consumer 's account is closed, they are still entitled to access the funds in the account. If the bank closes an account without providing proper notice, it must ensure that the account holder is able to retrieve their funds. This is especially important if the closure was not initiated due to fraud or a legitimate breach of contract.

4. Consumer Protection Under the D
odd-Frank Act The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010 established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to protect consumers from unfair or deceptive practices by financial institutions. The failure to notify a customer about the closure of an account and withholding access to their funds could be viewed as an unfair practice under this law, which is subject to investigation by the CFPB or relevant state authorities.

I was given case # XXXX and it was explained by the representative that my accounts would remain frozen and I would have to call in to make any transactions on my accounts. Also, Case # XXXX was added by the same representative at that time for additional security. 

Were those notes/ message placed on my account for any representative to see - as a warning? Apparently not- as Ally Bank has not protected my accounts nor my funds from fraud. 

On XX/XX/24, the fraudsters, who are on my computer, asked me to transfer {$9400.00} from savings to spending. When I called in, since I was previously told just XXXX days earlier that no transactions would be allowed - only the specific one that I requested when calling in - that representative unfroze my accounts against my knowledge or authorization. 

On XX/XX/24, the first fraudulent wire was sent - and verified by the wire department - even thought there should have been a message on the account the " I am a victim of identity theft and a money laundering scheme and I want my accounts frozen ''. I did not initiate the wire, request the wire, submit the wire form or whatever one does ( I've never done a wire ever ) I didn't even know the name of the bank. The fraudsters were on my computer doing everything and then would call and tell me exactly what to say to 'verify ' the wire. When one doesn't know what the name of the bank is - no suspicious activity there? I was told that I could not talk to anyone about this as the was an inside job with Ally Bank and the investigation would consider me to be a XXXX party if I was on my accounts. They locked my screen for days and threatened me with repeated messages to not talk to anyone. That would include the wire department when they called to verify the wire- as I believed they were the culprits. I was under increasing duress with each wire. On XX/XX/24, I called Ally Bank asking for the Fraud Department. When I was finally transferred to XXXX in the Fraud Department she wouldn't talk to me because I had my boss sitting with me at my desk ( 3rd party ). XXXX continued to say that there was a 3rd party and I said several times, " I have fraud on my account ''. XXXX hung up the phone- apparently without making any notes on my account or doing anything to protect my funds- as already XXXX had been fraudulently wired out. 

The fraudsters created and submitted the XXXX wire in the morning of XX/XX/24 - and called me to tell me what to sat when the wire department called. I received a phone call from someone at Ally Bank ( maybe wire department ) asking if I had made a transfer of XXXX from spending to savings. I said, " Uhhh, I will have to call you back '' as the fraudsters had done this. Remember, my computer is locked and I am repeatedly told to not say anything because this is an inside job - only the XXXX XXXX of these - and the other XXXX were people from Ally doing this. I did not call back and did not authorize the transfer of XXXX between accounts. When this last wire didn't go - I was told that i had to call Ally and find out why. No sign of suspicious or unusual activity there. What was the wire department looking for - but apparently there was no notes on my account from my initial message on XX/XX/24 " I am the victim of identity theft and a money laundering scheme and want my accounts frozen ''. Then another person called an asked if I use an XXXX and XXXX computer. I said yes - as the fraudsters were on my devices committing these fraudulent transactions. No suspicious or unusual activity when my funds are now wiped out in the matter of 3 days - and NO XXXX from Ally Bank thinks any of this is fraudulent. I have called XXXX times to Ally Bank and have been lied to by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX from the XXXX team told me on XX/XX/24 that she had good news after all of the bad news that I would be getting my funds back with interest by the end of next week ( XX/XX/XXXX ). 
Ally Bank must not have put any phone message notes on any of my accounts- because how could this been missed by the wire department, the fraud department ( XXXX ) and the front line employees who took my calls? Ally Bank does not train their employees - since no one asked me if there was fraud on my account, why I didn't know the name of the Bank on the first wire, why I never authorized the XXXX transfer on XX/XX/24. Ally Bank does not review the numerous phone calls of me stating what happened as I was threatened by the fraudsters repeatedly told I couldn't talk to anyone because it was an inside job. If I said anything l would considered the 3rd party and my computer was locked by them. I was under great duress and no one from Ally Bank asked a single qualifying question - especially with the XXXX wire when it took most of the day to send. Is not someone calling in asking why the wire not having been sent a red flag? 
On XX/XX/24, I called in to ask about the complaint that was supposedly still open and XXXX in the Fraud Prevention Department lied to me and said that my case was basically closed - and there wasn't a supervisor available. With intense pushback from me- if you had reviewed any of the recorded phone calls from XX/XX/24 - you would know full story. Ally Bank has XXXX XXXX XXXX because XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX said that wires were authorized. XXXX XXXX the Investigator has never returned my phone requests- yet a 'comprehensive " review has been done? Only completed with a goal in mind - XXXX Fraud Liability. However, XXXX from the escalation team said that there was fraud on my account- just not wire fraud. What is the fraud then? I want the truth- as Ally Bank has untrained, incompetent employees in several departments that have repeatedly lied and covered up the truth - only cherry picking XXXX phone calls for 'wire verification '. 

Remember, 'we are all better off with an ally '. I used to believe that but now worry how I will lose the remaining high XXXX figure funds still with Ally Bank.
